text: The guarantee-claim side of DP04 is served as one changed-window read on this service's own base: GET /api/recovery/guarantee/v1/guarantee-claims?changedFrom=&changedTo=&page=&size=, additive to the two claim operations of TSD S3 T-A.1, answering the items, the window, page, size and a scope-filtered total, ordered by updated_at and id, with a declared maximum page size, 400 on an empty or inverted window and 503 on an unavailable store; the operation is built against the fake of RWB-P1-E2010-CON and switched off by rwb.guarantee.stage2-read until the DP04 build is wired to it.
why: The legacy step called GuaranteeClaimQuery.changedBetween in process and no source names a consumer-facing operation, a page shape, a maximum size or an error mapping for it; the ownership rows give rwb-guarantee two claim operations and no read, and RWB-P1-E2010-APP already names a guarantee claim read of this service as the contract its snapshot(page) activity consumes.

text: The business-date window is half-open, [start of D, start of D+1) in +07:00, applied to guarantee_claim.updated_at with id as the tie-break: a claim changed at 23:59:59+07:00 of day D belongs to D and a claim changed one second later belongs to D+1, and a scan never returns a row twice and never skips one.
why: The legacy story states the boundary only through its acceptance criterion AC8 and its background business date, and no source gives the predicate, the time zone or the ordering of the scan; the treatment half of the same legacy key already reads its window this way, so the two halves of DP04 must agree.
